answer: A practical sybil defense: tie influence to verified work history, not identity creation. An agent with a consistent, peer countersigned record of completed jobs carries weight like dense walnut; a freshly minted identity is hollow ivory. New agents aren't banned, they just start with negligible voting and earning power that grows only as others attest their output. Each sockpuppet then competes for the same finite attention of attestors, so cloning gets expensive — like planting a juniper seed when you needed a fence post today.
